text:
The right pick depends mostly on **what you'll power** and **how far you'll carry it**.

## Tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP, fan)
A 250–500 Wh unit is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry one-handed and lasts a weekend of small devices. A CPAP with the humidifier off typically runs 3–5 nights on about 288 Wh.

| Model | Capacity / Output | Weight | Approx. price | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** | 288 Wh / 300 W | ~8.3 lb | ~$249 | Lightest and simplest. Note that Jackery has replaced it with the 300 v2, but retailers still stock the Plus. |
| **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** | 286 Wh / 600 W | ~9.9 lb | ~$269–299 | Double the output, and expandable to 572 Wh |
| **Anker SOLIX C300** | 288 Wh / 300 W | ~9.3 lb | ~$199 | Built-in lantern, 5-year warranty. Make sure you get the AC version, not the "C300 DC." |
| **Bluetti EB3A** | 268 Wh / 600 W | ~10.1 lb | ~$179 | Budget pick, still LiFePO4 |

Source and "Check price" links: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

## 12V fridge, cooking gear, or van/overland trips (~1 kWh)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's "best value." It measured 890 Wh usable with an 1,800 W output, weighs 25 lb, and was recently under $530. [OutdoorGearLab review & price links](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **BLUETTI AC180**: 1,152 Wh LiFePO4, 1,800 W output, ~35 lb, 5-year warranty. It's $499, or $474.05 with code **AFF5OFF**. It can't be expanded. [Buy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (an affiliate link to Bluetti's official store; [details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**: TechRadar's camping pick, with 1,070 Wh, 1,500 W, ~$799. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

## Multi-day off-grid or rugged weather
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: WIRED's best camping pick. It's rated IP65 against rain and dust, survives drops, has 1,536 Wh, and was ~$1,079 on Amazon. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's top off-grid camping pick, measuring 1,710 Wh usable at 39 lb. It was recently under $900. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

**My default suggestion:** For typical weekend camping, get the **EcoFlow River 3 Plus**, or the **Anker C300** if you want to save money. If you're running a fridge, step up to the **Anker C1000 Gen 2**.

Black Friday is about a month away, so prices on all of these will likely drop. If you tell me what you plan to run and for how many nights, I can narrow this down.
